findings.title: Effort stamping does not reliably distinguish sent from unresolved execution
findings.description:
D5 stamps effort after model resolution, although resolution does not establish that a provider request occurred. Conversely, it declares that cancelled actions and subprocesses without run state sent nothing; either can terminate after dispatch.

This undermines the architecture’s “Absent is not zero” principle and the slice plan’s requirement to record actual effort rather than a configured stand-in. Define the dispatch boundary that establishes effort sent, preserve that evidence through failure where possible, and treat missing evidence as unknown—not proof that nothing was sent. Cover pre-dispatch failure, mid-call cancellation, and subprocess termination in tests.

findings.title: Additional identity fields describe configuration rather than effective requests
findings.description:
D6 copies alias `tool_use` and `max_output_tokens` into config identity because they supposedly both change what is sent. That is not universally true: the referenced slice 175 explicitly states that SDK providers do not apply output-token budgets. Two SDK aliases with identical effective requests could therefore remain separate contestants solely because their unused budgets differ.

Cut these additional identity dimensions from this effort audit, retaining the required alias-independent grouping by model, profile, and effort sent. If broader request identity is necessary, specify and capture effective provider-applied values rather than raw alias settings.

Additional identity fields describe configuration rather than effective requests
